_meta.what: Static registry of every EXTERNAL tool the Zanmai distribution itself invokes or depends on. Derived from an audit of dist/, not from any machine.
_meta.ownership: Distribution material. Shipped and REPLACED on update. User-immune. It is maintained in lockstep: introducing a new external tool REQUIRES an entry here (a §3 doc-update rule, like manifest.yaml).
consumers: `zanmai.py tools doctor`, detect the whole set on this machine
`zanmai.py tools ensure <id>`, provision an on-demand tool at first use
an agent resolves invocation/presence/version per OS before any external call

tiers.prerequisite: Must exist up front; missing -> tell the user (guide). Never auto-installed.
tiers.on-demand: Provisioned at first use of the feature that needs it: detect -> fetch -> remember.
tiers.recommended: Accelerator only (brew/scoop/winget); never a hard dependency.
tiers.host-configured: MCP servers; host configures them, zero-install from Zanmai's point of view (LD6).

_meta.detect_rule: Never assume. Resolve invocation + presence + version + identity (a name can be a different program: on some machines grep is ugrep, find is bfs, and python is not python3). Presence is checked live per machine, never stored here.
_meta.verified_legend: os.<name>.verified=true = checked on real hardware (verified on macOS; windows/linux are DESIGNED until tested).
_meta.guide_note: install_hint.guide points at a per-OS help doc. These docs are STUBS for now (just the target path); the guided-help build is a later step (README/Wiki, plan Teil B).

cross_os.linux: DESIGNED, unverified. Invocation is essentially macOS's, both are Unix, so python3/ffmpeg/git/node/yt-dlp/c2patool/pdffonts/magick share binary names; the only real deltas are file-open (xdg-open vs open) and the secret store (secret-tool/libsecret vs Keychain), both already reflected. The venv path is identical (many distro pythons are also PEP-668 externally-managed, so venv is right there too). Provisioning is deliberately NOT automated: too many distros/package managers, and a Linux user installs an app themselves, Linux is a documented prerequisite, no binary auto-fetch.
cross_os.windows: DESIGNED, unverified, first idea, verify on a fresh Windows machine. Deltas: python is `py -3`/`python`, not python3; binaries carry `.exe` (shutil.which still resolves via PATHEXT); no Keychain, Credential Manager (cmdkey/PowerShell) or the .env fallback (likely cleaner for the signer key); file-open via os.startfile/`start`; recommender is winget (built into Win10+/11) or scoop; the venv python lives at Scripts\python.exe (already handled). The one part that must be Windows-native is the non-Python bootstrap (PowerShell vs Unix shell), pending the fresh-Windows test.

_meta.sizes: size_mb is the installed size measured on macOS 2026-08-27, per Homebrew cellar entry or per venv library including what it pulls in. Libraries share dependencies, so the total of a group is smaller than the sum of its parts: the eight Python libraries add up to 373 but measure 323 together. Shown to the user before anything is fetched, because a number nobody sees is not transparency.

ffmpeg.purpose: Video frames (Reed), video label burn and assembly (Loki), and converting a dropped voice note from whatever a phone recorded (m4a, aac, mp3, ogg) into the 16 kHz mono the transcriber needs.

c2patool.purpose: C2PA via CLI (alternative to the python lib).

whisper.purpose: Turns speech into text on this machine, with no network and no key, which is what a spoken journal entry needs. Used for a dropped voice note and for Reed's video and audio pipeline. Takes an initial prompt, which is how the vault's own names bias the recognition.

chromium.purpose: Turns Carol's designed HTML into an exact print-ready PDF. Safari has no background print path, so a Chromium-based engine is what renders the layout to A4.

install_hint.text: brew install --cask chromium (Chrome, Edge or Brave also work)

provision.note: any Chromium-based browser works (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Chromium, Vivaldi); detected cross-OS via PATH + per-OS app paths, not auto-fetched. Missing on macOS (Safari only) surfaces a clear install message; Windows usually has Edge preinstalled.

poppler.purpose: Turns a render into pixels and text so it can be measured rather than assumed (pdftoppm for coverage, bleed and the contact sheet; pdftotext to check the text arrived complete; pdffonts to check the fonts are embedded). Without it a document can be built but not verified.

ghostscript.purpose: Converts the final PDF to CMYK for a real press run (html skill). Only needed when the job is print production, not for a screen or RGB flyer.

c2pa_signer.purpose: Self-managed signing identity for the fallback / re-seal case (valid, not trust-listed).

provision.command: zanmai.py media signer ensure (generates via the cryptography lib and stores cert.pem/key.pem; media mark also establishes on demand)
provision.recipe: P-256 (prime256v1) key in PKCS#8 + cert with keyUsage=digitalSignature, EKU=emailProtection, CA:FALSE, AND subjectKeyIdentifier + authorityKeyIdentifier (c2pa REJECTS a signing cert lacking SKI/AKI, verified 2026-07-20).
provision.storage: user config dir OUTSIDE the vault (XDG_CONFIG_HOME/APPDATA), chmod 600, never in the vault (LD6).

secret_store.purpose: Hold connection secrets and the signer key outside the vault (LD6).
secret_store.fallback: gitignored .env outside the vault, chmod 600, masked.

connection_clis.purpose: Optional host CLIs Wong can bridge to, opt-in per use-case.

typst.purpose: Sets a document: real text flow across pages, a full-width block deferred to the next page while text keeps filling the current one, column balancing, hyphenation dictionaries, page numbers and bleed. The renderer for anything paged; a browser paginates a web page and has none of this.

install_hint.text: brew install typst, or let Zanmai fetch the pinned build
distro package typst, or let Zanmai fetch the pinned build
winget install Typst.Typst, or let Zanmai fetch the pinned build

provision.note: One self-contained binary per platform, which is why this tier fits it at all. A host copy that meets the pin is used as it stands; nothing is installed beside it. Identity is proven by running the binary and matching the pinned version, then by compiling the canary, so a half-unpacked archive fails at provisioning rather than during real work.

python_pptx.purpose: Reads and writes a native .pptx without opening PowerPoint: which layout a slide uses, whether its placeholders are filled, whether a run overrides the layout, which faces and colours are actually in the file. The deck's measurable checks run on the file, because no engine but PowerPoint itself renders a .pptx faithfully.

whisper-model.purpose: The weights whisper runs on. Nothing transcribes without one, so this is the first-use step for voice notes. `large-v3-turbo` is the default: strong on German and fast enough that a two-minute note is seconds rather than minutes. About 1.6 GB, fetched once, and it lives in the machine-local runtime folder so it never travels in a backup.

provision.note: One plain file, so it is fetched rather than unpacked, and it is proven by transcribing a second of silence with it: a file of the right size that does not load is the failure this catches. Machine-local on purpose, so it never travels in a backup.

install_hint.text: Zanmai fetches it: `tools ensure whisper-model`. One file of about 1.6 GB over HTTPS, once, into the vault's machine-local runtime folder. Nothing is unpacked and nothing is uploaded.

ffprobe.purpose: Reads how long a recording is, and whether a media file is what its name claims. Ships with ffmpeg; listed separately because it is invoked separately.

hyperframes.purpose: Builds a motion graphic from markup and renders it frame by frame in a headless browser, which is what lets a cut carry graphics at all. Fetched on first use of the motion skill and pinned to one version, because every graphic is tuned against one version's behaviour and a silent upgrade breaks renders that were already signed off.

provision.note: Needs node 22 or newer. Installed into the vault's runtime tree, not globally.

libreoffice.purpose: Renders a deck without opening PowerPoint: one picture per slide, and the PDF export of a finished deck. The only way a run can look at a slide it built instead of trusting its own description of it.

install_hint.text: brew install --cask libreoffice, or download from libreoffice.org
apt install libreoffice-impress, or the distro package

provision.note: 804 MB and a full office suite: too big to fetch behind the user's back, and there is no single-binary build. Named with its size at the first render that needs it, and at setup as one of the ones they install.

capabilities._meta: Per-expert, per-path REQUIRED tool ids. `tools preflight <expert> --capability <cap>` gates only on the required set, so a job takes only what that path needs (a screen flyer over html needs the renderer, not the Affinity MCP). Without --capability, preflight falls back to the expert's full needed_by (coarse). Optional refinements stay in needed_by and are surfaced by the expert, not gated. A capability under `shared` belongs to no single expert and is resolved for any of them that does not define its own: motion graphics are needed by whoever produces timed visuals, a cut today and a web page tomorrow, and a copy per expert is how two copies drift apart.

python_venv_provisioner.prefer: uv (fast, can also supply a pinned Python without admin)
python_venv_provisioner.floor: stdlib `python3 -m venv` (ensurepip present), no hard uv dependency
python_venv_provisioner.note: system python3 is often EXTERNALLY-MANAGED (PEP 668); a venv sidesteps that
